'''Veeth Drellik''' was a [[Tarsunt]] [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. In [[132 BBY]], he was informed by [[Senator]] [[Worus Rayencourt]] of the [[Jedi Order]]'s lack of transparency surrounding an internal [[Indara's murder|murder]] investigation led by [[Jedi Master]] [[Vernestra Rwoh]]. Rwoh was later called before a [[Galactic Senate|Senate]] tribunal in the [[Jedi Diplomatic Tower]] led by Drellik to provide an update on the investigation but lied to them, claiming that a Jedi Master named [[Sol]] had gone rogue and committed the [[Death|murders]] before ending his own life.

==Biography==
{{Quote|I have reported your lack of transparency to Chancellor Drellik. He may invite you to a Senate tribunal for an update. I hope for your sake, you have this suspect in custody by then.|Rayencourt mentions Drellik to Vernestra Rwoh|audio=Raynecourt-Drellik-TheAcolyte.flac|<ref name="Acolyte" />}}
[[File:TenseMeeting-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Vernestra Rwoh and Worus Rayencourt stare each other down in a confrontation on Coruscant.|Drellik called a tribunal over Worus Rayncourt's concerns.]] 
Veeth Drellik<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> was a [[Tarsunt]] who served as [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]<ref name="Acolyte" /> during the later [[Standard year|years]] of the [[High Republic Era]]<ref name="DB" /> at a [[time]] when [[the galaxy]] was blossoming with promise.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2025 Topps Star Wars Chrome|cardname=#111 - Chancellor Drellik|link=https://www.ebay.com/itm/326798109366}}
*{{Databank|chancellor-drellik|Chancellor Drellik}}</ref> Under his watchful leadership, representatives from all corners of the [[galaxy]] served in<ref name="DB" /> an impressive<ref name="Topps" /> [[Galactic Senate]] as the Republic blossomed.<ref name="DB" />

In [[132 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TheAcolyteDate}}</ref> [[Senator]] [[Worus Rayencourt]]<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> learned that the [[Jedi Order]] was investigating a [[Indara's murder|murder]] internally without informing the Republic, playing in to his wishes for it to be externally reviewed.<ref name="Acolyte" /> Rayencourt reported the Order's lack of transparency to Drellik before confronting [[Jedi Master]] [[Vernestra Rwoh]], who was leading the investigation, and informing<ref name="Acolyte" /> her<ref name="Acolyte AD">{{Acolyte|The Acolyte (episode)}} {{AD|Disney+}}</ref> that the chancellor may summon her to a tribunal for an update on the investigation. After the investigation had [[Duel on Brendok|concluded]],<ref name="Acolyte" /> Drellik convened a formal tribunal in the [[Jedi Diplomatic Tower]] on<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> the Republic [[capital]]<ref name="Acolyte AD" /> [[Coruscant]] to review the situation<ref name="Acolyte" /> and summoned Rwoh to give a report. The [[Jedi]] reported that Jedi Master [[Sol]] had gone rogue and [[Death|killed]] three other Jedi in order to cover up the four's involvement in the [[Mission to Brendok|destruction]] of a [[Brendok coven|Force cult]] on the [[planet]] [[Brendok]] [[148 BBY|sixteen years]] earlier. However, this was a lie,<ref name="Acolyte" /> as the three other Jedi had been killed by the [[Sith assassin|assassin]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya]]<ref name="Lost / Found">{{Acolyte|Lost / Found}}</ref><ref name="Revenge / Justice">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> and her [[Sith Master]], the individual known as [[the Stranger]].<ref name="Day">{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}}</ref>

[[File:Drellik-Tribunal-TheAcoylte.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Vernestra Rwoh stands at the end of a long conference table, with senators stood along each side staring at her. At the opposite end of the table, Veeth Drellik stands in a blue robe with his hands clasped.|Drellik heard from Vernestra Rwoh at the Senate tribunal and was satisfied with her report.]]
Upon hearing the report, Rayencourt pushed for an external review of the Jedi to begin immediately, claiming there was no time for a full Senate vote, but Drellik questioned Rwoh further and asked what had become of Sol. Rwoh then reported that they had found Sol dead on Brendok and claimed that he had ended his own life, although in truth Sol's former [[Padawan]] [[Verosha Aniseya]] had murdered him.<ref name="Acolyte" /> Drellik was satisfied with this conclusion.<ref name="Topps" />

==Personality and traits==
Drellik gave the benefit of the doubt to the Jedi Order, coming to rely on Rwoh's candor, but was willing to give time to Rayencourt's concerns.<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> An elegant individual,<ref name="Topps" /> he had black [[eye]]s, brown skin, and graying brown [[Hair|fur]], dying his beard to look more youthful.<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> He stood 1.63 [[meter]]s tall.<ref name="DB" />

==Equipment==
At the Senate tribunal, Drellik wore a blue [[Clothing|robe]] with golden detailing and a high collar.<ref name="Acolyte" /> He also had an [[orthoclase]] signet of office on his left middle [[Limb|finger]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Drellik appeared in "[[The Acolyte (episode)|The Acolyte]],"<ref name="Acolyte" /> the eighth episode of the [[Disney+]] live-action series of the [[Star Wars: The Acolyte|same name]], which aired on [[July 16]], [[2024]].<ref name="D23">{{D23|url=everything-coming-to-disney-in-july|text=Everything Coming to Disney+ in July 2024}}</ref> Two pieces of concept art of the tribunal room both titled "The Senate Floor" by production designer [[Kevin Jenkins]] show the figure stood at the head of the table as more [[human]] in appearance rather than Tarsunt.<ref name="ArtOf">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''</ref> He was performed by [[Tom Wilton]].<ref name="Acolyte" /> Drellik's first name was revealed to be Veeth in the [[2025]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" />
